title: Fit model state into each accelerator
description: Change the model, cluster, reserve, and sharding stage. The result exposes which bytes stay replicated and which bytes divide across the data-parallel group.

strategies.label: FSDP / ZeRO Stage 3
strategies.detail: Shard parameters, gradients, and optimizer state across the data-parallel group.
strategies.communication: Parameters are all-gathered for computation and gradients are reduce-scattered. Peak memory can exceed the persistent estimate while full parameter groups are live.
strategies.tradeoff: Use full sharding when replicated model state does not fit. It saves the most persistent memory but makes parameter communication and wrapping policy part of the critical design.

strategies.label: DistributedDataParallel
strategies.detail: Replicate parameters, gradients, and Adam state on every data-parallel rank.
strategies.communication: Gradient buckets are all-reduced during backward. Each rank ends with the same averaged gradients and applies the optimizer update to its local replica.
strategies.tradeoff: Prefer DDP when a complete replica fits comfortably. It keeps execution simple, but adding ranks does not reduce per-GPU model-state memory.

strategies.label: ZeRO Stage 1
strategies.detail: Partition the FP32 master weights and Adam moments while keeping parameters and gradients replicated.
strategies.communication: Gradients remain replicated, while each rank owns only its optimizer-state partition and exchanges updated parameter information after the local optimizer work.
strategies.tradeoff: Stage 1 is a smaller operational step from DDP, but it cannot solve memory pressure dominated by replicated parameters or gradients.

strategies.label: ZeRO Stage 2
strategies.detail: Partition gradients and optimizer state while keeping low-precision parameters replicated.
strategies.communication: Gradient ownership is reduce-scattered and updated parameter state is synchronized across ranks. Parameters still consume replicated memory.
strategies.tradeoff: Stage 2 removes most persistent redundancy without parameter all-gathers, but it still cannot fit a parameter set larger than one accelerator.
